review_locator: PMCID:PMC6001902, Tuning the Cytokine Responses: An Update on Interleukin (IL)-4 and IL-13 Receptor Complexes; PMCID:PMC3981547, Structural Biology of Shared Cytokine Receptors
primary_title: Tuning sensitivity to IL-4 and IL-13: differential expression of IL-4Ralpha, IL-13Ralpha1, and gammac regulates relative cytokine sensitivity
decision_basis: The reviews identify the type II IL-4 receptor as IL-4Rα/IL-13Rα1; the primary macrophage/monocyte study distinguishes this complex from the γc-containing type I receptor and links receptor-chain composition to IL-4 signaling sensitivity.
limitations_preserved: Preserve IL-4 type I versus type II receptor usage, IL-13Rα1 versus γc partner, cell-type-dependent receptor abundance, and STAT6 functional context; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3471675, Structural Insights into the Common γ-Chain Family of Cytokines and Receptors from the Interleukin-7 Pathway; PMCID:PMC6120701, The Common Cytokine Receptor γ Chain Family of Cytokines
primary_title: Reconstitution of a functional interleukin (IL)-7 receptor demonstrates that the IL-2 receptor gamma chain is required for IL-7 signal transduction
decision_basis: The reviews identify IL-7Rα/γc as the IL-7 receptor complex; the primary reconstitution study shows that co-expression of IL-2Rγ with IL-7R is required for IL-7-dependent reporter activation and that both cytoplasmic domains are needed for maximal signaling.
limitations_preserved: Preserve IL-7Rα/γc heterodimer and reconstituted reporter context; the cited study establishes functional receptor-complex signaling rather than a solved ligand-bound ternary structure; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6120701, The Common Cytokine Receptor γ Chain Family of Cytokines; PMCID:PMC3981547, Structural Biology of Shared Cytokine Receptors
primary_title: Sharing of the IL-2 receptor gamma chain with the functional IL-9 receptor complex
decision_basis: The reviews identify IL-9Rα/γc as the functional IL-9 receptor; the primary cross-linking and antibody-blockade study places γc in the IL-9 receptor complex and shows that it is required for IL-9-dependent proliferation and growth-signal transduction.
limitations_preserved: Preserve IL-9Rα/γc functional-complex assignment and antibody/cross-linking model; do not infer a unique STAT branch or SCI immune-cell weighting; no terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3981547, Structural Biology of Shared Cytokine Receptors; PMCID:PMC5983187, Role of the β Common (βc) Family of Cytokines in Health and Disease
primary_title: Human interleukin-3 (IL-3) induces disulfide-linked IL-3 receptor alpha- and beta-chain heterodimerization, which is required for receptor activation but not high-affinity binding
decision_basis: The reviews identify IL-3Rα/βc as the human IL-3 receptor complex; the primary study shows IL-3 induces disulfide-linked IL-3 receptor α/β-chain heterodimerization required for receptor activation, while distinguishing activation from high-affinity binding.
limitations_preserved: Preserve human βc/IL-3Rα topology and the distinction between receptor activation and high-affinity ligand binding; mouse IL-3-specific β-chain usage is a species caveat; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5983187, Role of the β Common (βc) Family of Cytokines in Health and Disease; PMCID:PMC11102305, Structure of the Interleukin-5 receptor complex exemplifies the organizing principle of common beta cytokine signaling
primary_title: Structure of the interleukin-5 receptor complex exemplifies the organizing principle of common beta cytokine signaling; Structural basis of interleukin-5 dimer recognition by its α receptor
decision_basis: The reviews identify IL-5Rα/βc as the IL-5 receptor complex; primary structural and biochemical studies resolve IL-5/IL-5Rα/βc assembly and show receptor-complex organization, ligand-receptor interfaces, and signaling-complex architecture.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the IL-5 homodimer, IL-5Rα specificity, βc shared-subunit and higher-order oligomerization context; no generic IL-3/GM-CSF equivalence, SCI, or terminal-TF inference.
